Suppose you're in a highly dense urban area, no possibility of retreating to the wilds nor building a safe house. You are prepping alone but have access to decent gear and firearms. This also means that when SHTF, you'll have to carry your whole shit with you since you don't have a BOL (Bug-Out location). We're also assuming that this is a highly hostile environment with martial law in place and you'll likely have to keep moving around.

Given this scenario...

How much gear / ammo is too much?

What's your preferred backpack size?

Assuming you carry military MREs (more calories per pack) how many should you stuff in your BOB (Bug-Out Bag)?

How complete should your first aid kit be? which medicines should you carry?

I'm probably forgetting a lot of important questions, but that's what i can think of for now.

dense Urban area, no possibility of retreat or fortifying

It doesn't matter, in that scenario, because you're likely going to die with 99.9%of the others in that situation.

It's nothing on you, it's just that you're ruling out all your options. If you can't run, can't fight, can't stand a siege, no amount of prepping will save you. But, let's give it a try.

So. Pack. You're in a metropolis, so you should have easy access to some sort of store selling hiking equipment somewhere. If it's not post apocalyptic, then you can find something you'll like. If it is post, then just grab a school book bag and take off. It'll work just fine, for awhile.

How much gear/ammo is too much? That depends on what you need. In a city, you can do without certain things. You won't need much fire starting stuff, carry a lighter or 3. You should have relatively easy access to water for the first few days, at least, so store as much as you're able in whatever location you happen to be at. Which means iodine tablets. Cheap if you get it beforehand, and easy to carry. If you can't, can always put a few drops of bleach in the container. Neither taste great, they keep it potable for awhile. You'll find a lot of containers on your way, it's a city after all.

Probably won't need too much shelter, either. Grab 3-4 space blankets now, and find a place to hole up while you can. While you can, cause your mission should be to GTFO of that City. Which brings me to...

Maps. A paper fucking map of your state, at least. All fifty, or whatever, if you're feeling adventurous when it hits the fan. Gps and cell phones will be good for a couple days, but a map will be your best friend in a week. Go get one, right now, and learn to read it if you don't.

So. Right now, we've got water, shelter, fire and a map. Not bad for a pack that probably weighs all of 2 pounds so far. Now onto food.

This is the biggest hassle. No matter what, it's big, it's bulky, or you have to carry 57 if it's a bar. Which, honestly, it should be. If you don't want to spend money on high end stuff with 3000cal/bar, you can go buy a couple packs of those dry granola bars. They taste like crap, but they're like 300 calories, light, and individually packaged. Box has 6, weighs maybe a pound and they'll stay good pretty much as long as they're dry.

Next is your old friend spaghetti. Take a few packs, vacuum seal it, and you'll have a nice carb source if you can ever spare 15m to stop, boil some water, and throw on some spices.

Yeah, spices. Nothing will make you feel more human than having a hot meal that tastes not bad. Just carry some salt, pepper, maybe store cayenne. It's your choice, but bring something.

So we're probably up to, what? 6-7 pounds maybe? That's food, water, fire, shelter, and the ever useful map. Things are looking pretty good for your ammo. Of Which, IMO, you should carry as much as you feel you can. You don't want your pack to be any more than 20-25 pounds, trust me, but you gotta carry ammo. Which means .22, 9mm and shit, can't remember NATO caliber. 7.62x39? Those are, pretty much, the most common calibers in the US area. Carry a lot of .22, that should be your go to round. Quiet, accurate, and still lethal. Less 9mm, because it's loud and you probably won't have ear protection, which will be pretty crucial if you have any extended firefights. Less NATO caliber for the same reason, and that you probably won't be shooting 200yds in a city. Your ammo ratio should be something like 10:3:1 or higher, cause you seriously should just carry a ton of .22 for your pistol and rifle.

I'm losing track here, lol. So, food, shelter, water, fire, weapon, ammo, map... Oh! A knife. Not a machete, though you should have one in your pack, but a knife. Fixed blade, probably 10 inches, and a sheath to hook it to your belt.

And medicine. That's tricky. Full of expiration dates, and the general fact there's just so much to choose from. Get an Israeli bandage online, and some of that powder that promotes clotting. Other that that, just gauze, bandages, some antiseptic, and duct tape. Anything else you can find along the way, when you come to a pharmacy. Grab the stuff that ends in '-illin' like amoxicillin, penicillin, etc. That's a general clue it's antibiotic in nature. Painkillers are also handy, for when you have to keep moving no matter what.

All in all, you'll probably be looking at a 25 pound backpack. If you've never been hiking before, I suggest you go get one and load it up with crap until your bathroom scale says it's around 25, go out to your yard, and practice running around with it. It's a lot harder than you would think, and much more painful, so you'll see why I've left out a lot of the crap like I've got in mine. It's only 35-40lbs, but it's got a detachable part that's got emergency emergency supplies in that I can take and run if the occasion arises.

I'm probably leaving stuff out too, but I'm just here to put out some ideas. Feel free to leave ideas of your own, or ways to lighten it further.

Oh! Army surplus waterproof bags. Get a couple, they're cheap as hell and worth every penny. And string or Paracord!

How much gear / ammo is too much?

That's more a physical conditioning question, if anything. You should aim to be able to carry fifty to sixty pounds on your back, while walking for a mile and a half distance and/or thirty minutes. Once you can do that, the question becomes organization of your bugout bag and there are plenty of folks who've plugged tips on that end.

What's your preferred backpack size?

Depends on the person, their physical condition, and what their priorities are. Some can handle large heavy weight, some can't. If you've got to bug out, you'll be more concerned with maximizing the paced distance you can travel from the danger.

Assuming you carry military MREs (more calories per pack) how many should you stuff in your BOB (Bug-Out Bag)?

I'd travel with three days worth of MRE's. I can restock when I reach my bug-out location. If restocking isn't an option, then I'd want to carry tools to help me effectively gather and forage.

How complete should your first aid kit be? which medicines should you carry?

Depends on what sort of injuries you anticipate experiencing and what pre-existing health issues you have. If you need meds to maintain maximum health, then a 90 day supply should do you well. Some meds are considered controlled substances and physicians aren't allowed to give you more than you can consume at that time, so you might have to ration your consumption to build that 90 day supply.
